IncidentBot: Incident RESOLVED for routing-pipeline (svc: inference-router). Mitigation applied: fallback to model-variant B + autoscale bump. Root cause: routing compile backlog leading to request drops. Postmortem in progress: https://redwood.incidents/1768001234

Lia (CS): Thanks — I'm preparing an external debrief for the affected customer (Privileged account). Need to confirm exact customer impact window and approximate % of requests that errored. cc @Tom (Eng Oncall) @Sam (Customer)

Tom (Eng Oncall): Timeline from infra: error spike starts 2024-10-22 15:12 UTC, peak 15:18, mitigation started 15:24, fully resolved 15:29. Approx failed requests ~4.6% of their routed traffic during the 17-minute window. Root cause detail: compile backlog on the routing compiler when model config refresh coincided with a large affinity shuffle.

Sam (Customer): Got it. Customer cares about duration, requests lost, and whether any data left company network. They asked for an exec-friendly summary + a note on SLA credits.

Lia (CS): Drafting proposed customer-facing paragraph — please confirm wording and whether we can include a rough credit calc.

Jordan (PM): Keep the external text short, then attach a timeline appendix. For credits: use their committed monthly reserved tokens + measured error rate over impact window. Ops can give final $ amount.

Anya (Security): Confirming no data exfiltration. All traffic remained within the customer's VPC endpoint; no logs sent to third parties. Recommend we include a line: "No customer data was exported."

Tom (Eng Oncall): Quick technical blurb for the appendix: 
```
Timeline (UTC):
15:12 - routing compiler backlog begins (config refresh + affinity shuffle)
15:18 - request error rate spikes (avg 4.6% for this customer)
15:24 - fallback routing policy engaged (variant B)
15:29 - autoscaler completed burst and error rate returned to baseline
Mitigation: routed to compatible model-variant + increased pool size; backlog drained.
```

Lia (CS): Proposed external paragraph (v1):
```
On 2024-10-22 between 15:12–15:29 UTC we experienced an availability degradation affecting inference requests for your account. During the window we observed an elevated error rate (~4.6%) caused by an internal routing compilation backlog. We mitigated the issue by routing requests to a compatible model variant and scaling capacity; the service returned to normal at 15:29 UTC. No customer data left your VPC. We will follow up with a detailed timeline and proposed corrective actions.
```

Sam (Customer): That reads well. Could we add a short line about credits? The customer will expect numbers.

Lia (CS): Suggested credit sentence (v1): "Based on your committed capacity and the measured error rate during the impact window, we estimate a one-time credit equivalent to X% of monthly reserved capacity billing; Ops will confirm the exact credit amount."

Jordan (PM): Action items: 1) Engineering to finalize timeline & failure counts (Tom) 2) Security to sign off on data statement (Anya) 3) CS to send exec summary + appendix (Lia) 4) Finance/Ops to compute tentative credit (Sam to request) 5) Follow-up postmortem + preventive actions (Jordan). Please add owners to calendar invite.

Tom (Eng Oncall): I can finalize counts by EOD UTC. Attaching quick grep results: `grep -c "error: routing" /var/log/router/2024-10-22.log` -> 3,412 errors for that customer ID during window. Baseline calls ~74k, so ~4.6%.

Anya (Security): Signed off on "no data exported" wording. Recommend we add: "We rotated service-side TLS certs for the routing plane as a precaution" (note: rotation occurred after resolution).

Lia (CS): I'll send the customer-facing email once Tom posts final counts and Ops confirms credit. Draft below — please comment inline if wording is problematic.
```
Subject: Incident summary — 2024-10-22 routing incident
Hi <Customer Contacts>,

On 2024-10-22 we experienced a short availability degradation for inference requests to your account between 15:12–15:29 UTC. During that period, a small portion of requests (approximately 4.6%) returned errors due to an internal routing compiler backlog. We mitigated the issue by temporarily routing requests to a compatible model variant and scaling capacity; service returned to normal by 15:29 UTC. No customer data left your network. We will provide a detailed timeline and next steps for prevention, and will follow up with a proposed credit for the affected window.

Please let us know if you'd like a meeting to walk through the timeline.

Best,
Lia (Customer Success)
```

Jordan (PM): Looks good. Small edit: replace "small portion" with the exact percent when Tom confirms. Also attach the appendix as a PDF with the detailed timeline and engineering notes.

Sam (Customer): I'll flag the meeting option as optional — customer typically wants the credit number first. Sam will ping Ops to prioritize credit calc.

Lia (CS): Thanks team. Will hold sending until final numbers and Ops note. Tentative send window tomorrow morning 09:00 UTC unless objected. :white_check_mark:
